title: feat(types): NamedListView mirrors spec 18's list-view requiredPermissions — no client gate
body:
Fixes #12341
Clause-②: yes

The objectui half of objectstack#22611 ruling A: `@object-ui/types` mirrors the list view's audience key `requiredPermissions` from `@objectstack/spec` 18. ⛔ No client-side gate is added. The server enforces the key (objectstack PR #22731) and the console surfaces its refusal (objectui#12112).

## What changed

- **`NamedListView` declares `requiredPermissions`** (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts`), typed by reference as `ListViewSchema['requiredPermissions']`. That member is the spec slot, taken by `specFieldsExcept` in the zod mirror, so the type is `string[] | undefined`, the same as the spec's `ListView['requiredPermissions']`.
- **Where the mirror was missing (measured on origin/main 065a1cf):** three faces of this package carry a list view. Two of them already had the key by reference. The `list-view` node (`ListViewSchema`) takes every spec key it does not override, and `list-view-spec-parity.test.ts` asserts that. `ObjectViewSchema.listViews` has been the spec's `ObjectListViewSchema` record since objectui#7928. Only the hand-written `NamedListView` lacked the key. objectui#12030 had pinned it there as `PENDING_SERVER_ENFORCED_DECLARATION`.
- **That pin is flipped, not duplicated** (`object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts`). The "narrower than the protocol" set is now `[]`. A declared member that no renderer reads would otherwise land in bucket ①, whose emptiness means "implementation owed". A server-enforced gate owes the renderer nothing, so the census gets a fifth bucket, `BUCKET_SERVER_ENFORCED_UNREAD = ['requiredPermissions']`. The partition is now 0 + 8 + 11 + 2 + 1 = 22 unread. Declared members go from 64 to 65, read members stay at 43, and the loose-regex count goes from 73 to 74 (the gap stays at 9). Bucket ① asserts that it holds exactly the server-enforced bucket and nothing else.
- **New pins** (`list-view-required-permissions-12341.test.ts`), accept and refuse on every face. Type-level: the member on all three faces equals the spec's `string[] | undefined`. On `NamedListView`, a bare string and a number list are each a `@ts-expect-error`. Runtime: the `list-view` mirror accepts and keeps a capability list, and refuses a string, a number list, an object and a boolean at the key, after a base-only parse control. `ObjectViewSchema.listViews` accepts the key and refuses a bare string at `listViews.legal_desk.requiredPermissions`.
- Changeset `.changeset/12341-list-view-required-permissions.md`: `@object-ui/types` minor. The published accept set widens.

## Widening, measured on the built declaration closure

`pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`, then read `packages/types/dist/objectql.d.ts`: `export interface NamedListView` gains exactly one member, `requiredPermissions?: ListViewSchema['requiredPermissions'];` (dist line 291 of the interface block). A probe compiled against `dist/index` with `tsc --strict` (exit 0) checks three things: the member equals `string[] | undefined`, `{ label, requiredPermissions: ['a.b'] }` is accepted, and `requiredPermissions: 'a.b'` is refused. Nothing else in the published surface moved. `ListViewSchema` and `ObjectViewSchema['listViews']` already carried the key.

## Reverse verification (a one-time proof, no permanent file)

The fix was committed first (4f01c04). Then `ablation-replace.mjs --delete` removed the declaration line (anchor 1 to 0, blob 76eef18c1220 to 0270a098714c), with this result:
- `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` went red with 3 errors in the new test file: `Property 'requiredPermissions' does not exist on type 'NamedListView'`.
- vitest on the two files went red, 7 failed / 230 passed. The failures were the census count, the declared-set equality, the instrument agreement, the partition, the per-member UNREAD row, the narrower-than-protocol zero and the bucket ① reading.
- Restore: blob back to 76eef18c1220 (equal to HEAD), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- The 12341 runtime tests stayed green under the ablation, as expected: the zod faces already carried the key.

## The one measurement the card asks for: the D4 viewer

**Answer:** yes, the console offers such a view. No, opening it does not answer `403`, so objectui#12112's surface is never reached.

- **Server:** `/meta/object` serves an object WHOLE to a caller ADR-0106 D4 exempts. See objectstack `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:1657` on origin/main b5b1bf72: `if (!sysPerms || isObjectSchemaMaskExempt(ctx)) return serve(document);`. Its stated reason is that a pruned load saved back would delete the withheld list views. Every other caller gets `filterObjectListViewsForUser` (lines 768-772).
- **Console listing:** `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:2335-2336` builds the switcher tabs from `objectDef.listViews` (`buildViewTabs({ definedViews: objectDef.listViews … })`). No audience check is applied there, and none should be.
- **Console opening:** the by-name probe runs only when the requested view MISSED the tab list (`ObjectView.tsx:2441-2455`, `missedViewName` then `useMetaItemRefusal('view', …)`). A D4 viewer's gated view is in the list, so it resolves, renders and never asks. The refusal face (`ObjectView.tsx:3844-3848`, `view-access-denied`) is not reached. In any case the server has no by-name `/meta/view` item for an object's own list view that it could refuse.
- **Already pinned:** `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.viewRefusal-12112.test.tsx:221-230`, the case "D4 (measured): an object's own list view served to its editor is listed and opens — no client rule hides or refuses it". In that case the probe is not called and no `view-access-denied` face appears.
- **Reading:** this is not a data leak. The records come from the caller's own object read permissions, and a D4 caller may edit the schema. It is an audience mismatch: an object's editor is offered, at runtime, views authored for another audience. Any fix belongs on the SERVER, and ⛔ not in a client gate. A proposed shape is for the plain runtime read to prune for D4 callers too, and to keep the whole document for the authoring doors (draft, layered or diff reads), which is the split the `app: 'author-exempt'` policy already makes. That is an objectstack decision, raised in the report's `open_questions`. Nothing in this PR touches it.

## Gates (worktree HEAD 9e6cb65)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (tsc + examples + `tsconfig.test.json`; `--listFiles` counts both touched test files in): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`: 378 files / 10262 tests passed.
- `pnpm turbo run build --concurrency=2 --filter='@object-ui/plugin-view^...'` (15/15) and then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-view type-check`: exit 0. plugin-view is the one package whose tests import `NamedListView` as a type. Other mentions (app-shell, data-objectstack, console) are in comments only.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the 3 touched `.ts` files: 0 errors. There are 27 warnings, all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` lines outside the diff. The config is root `eslint.config.js` and is not type-aware (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so the diff cannot move any verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`: all exit 0. `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` and `check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0.
- `check:spec-floors`: exit 1, the known failure on main ("The scan collapsed: 0 package(s) declare @objectstack/spec …"). objectui#12334 carries it, and it is not touched here. `check:doc-types` was not run because no docs changed. objectui has no `check:nul-bytes` script, so a control-byte grep over the 4 touched files was run instead: 0 hits.

## Acceptance notes

- The `NamedListView` docblock still says its fate "follows objectui#7924", and this PR does not change that.
- The spec's shared description still says the gate "is not enforced yet". Per triage, that sentence is the spec owner's to fix.
- The census's failure message still points at `.changeset/object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md`, which no longer exists (it was consumed at release). Only its member count was corrected here.

The session for this work is `https://claude.ai/code/session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`.
